slice: S7 - Stage 2: in-place resume (resume_from_fold, claim/consume gating, authority narrowing, ledger-fed closers, gateway loop-vs-segment choice)
summary: ConsumeApproval is the one gate against double execution. It is a permanent compare-and-set on approvals.consumed_at, so a second click with another claim token is refused. The fold claim is only a 120 s lease on state, so it runs second, under the same claim token. Resume order is consume, authority check, claim, fold checks, ledger read, decide, apply authority, first checkpoint save, loop. Any restore failure after a won consume falls back to stage 1 using the already-held consume. A widened authority, a held claim or a failed consume is a typed refusal with no fallback. The gateway consumes before it opens the SSE stream, which is what turns the loser of two parallel continues into an HTTP 409 (distinct claim tokens only). The design also surfaced four existing gaps, listed in risks: Authority::narrows treats an unspecified rung as the narrowest rung, stage 1 runs under the request's rung, floor and plan mode instead of the snapshot's, the segment number is hard-coded to 2, and ledger reserve ignores created=false.
approach:
DECISIONS (all grounded in code read this session; see unverified items in open_questions)

A. THE GATE
- ConsumeApproval (session-core orchestration_store::consume_approval, CONSUME_APPROVAL_SQL: UPDATE approvals ... WHERE status='granted' AND continuation_mode<>'' AND consumed_at IS NULL) is the single authority gate. It is permanent, row-locked and bound to org, run and user, and it is the only thing that authorises the released call. A second consumer with a different claim token reads consumed_at set and gets already_consumed && !same_claim, so it is refused. The same token replays (same_claim=true); that replay is what makes a retry after a dropped response safe.
- ClaimLoopCheckpoint (loop_checkpoint::claim) is only a lease that grants ownership of the fold. It moves paused or parked to resuming for 120 s. It expires, and a resuming row with an expired lease can be claimed again, so it cannot be the double-execution gate on its own.
- Order is CONSUME FIRST, CLAIM SECOND, same claim_token for both. Reasons: (1) consume has no side effect except spending the click, and it fails before anything is taken; (2) claim-first would leave the fold in resuming for 120 s when the consume then fails (expired or denied), and the user's retry would see a misleading 'in progress'; (3) after a won consume a fallback to stage 1 is always possible because stage 1 re-uses the held consume. Stage 1's own consume would be a same_claim replay, so the fallback re-uses the already-parsed Consumed value and makes NO second consume RPC.
- Failure matrix:
  1. consume refused: typed refusal, nothing claimed, fold untouched and still paused.
  2. consume ok, authority refused: typed refusal BEFORE the claim, so no lease is taken. The approval is spent; the same-token retry hits the same refusal. This is intended: a widened request never runs.
  3. consume ok, claim returns Aborted loop_checkpoint_claim_held (NEW code: state=resuming, claim_token_hash equals this token's hash, lease live): typed refusal continue_in_progress, no fallback, because the first continuation is alive.
  4. consume ok, claim refused for any other reason (not_claimable, disabled, did not authenticate, malformed, transport error): fall back to stage 1. A transport error is ambiguous (the claim may have committed), but falling back is still safe: only the consume-gated call runs, and the fold stays resuming under our token, so a duplicate same-token request gets claim_held. DURABLE_MUTATION_FORBIDDEN (ZDR or waived run) is fatal and passed through (DEC-32: waived is treated as ZDR for folds).
  5. claim ok, then a restore check fails (prompt drift, pending mismatch, ledger read failure, and so on): fall back to stage 1. The fold is NOT closed. The fallback segment's first fold save uses expected_seq = claimed seq, which clears the claim and keeps the chain.
  6. everything ok but the first checkpoint save fails: typed refusal resume_checkpoint_unavailable. No dispatch has happened and the lease expires after 120 s, so the same-token retry works.
  7. Crash after consume, or after claim and before any save: same-token retry re-consumes (replay), re-claims after lease expiry, and re-runs. A different token is refused as already_consumed, and the run waits for the recovery worker (S8 park TTL or outcome_unknown). Mitigation is client-side: the SPA must reuse one claim token per approval_id on retry.
- Second-line guards behind consume: (a) the fold lease, with the superseding rule below; (b) effect-ledger reserve with created=false, new in this slice (effect::reserve returns Created or AlreadyReserved; AlreadyReserved on an effectful call means an earlier attempt may have started it, so it is closed with CloserKind::UnknownOutcome and not run).
- LEASE HOLE AND SUPERSEDING RULE: the claim lease (120 s) is shorter than a long tool call. A same-token retry could re-claim a resuming row with an expired lease while the first loop still runs. Rule: the resumed round must save a pre_effect fold (writer seeded with seq=claimed.seq, segment_no=fold.segment_no+1) BEFORE phase-2 dispatch. save() upserts the row to state=active and clears the claim, so the row stops being claimable by pause_ref. Active rows are claimable only after 900 s without a write. In-place resume therefore requires EXECUTION_LOOP_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED (the S6 switch) as well as EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED. If the S6 switch is off, 'loop' is downgraded to 'segment'.

B. resume_from_fold: EXACT ORDER (execution-core, called from run_agent_with_route where prepare_resume is called today)
 0. Already true at the gRPC boundary: delegated bearers; enforce_persistence_free_execution(req.zdr, 'agent_run') refuses ZDR before anything; enforce_resume validates mode in {segment, loop}, approval_id and claim_token.
 1. in_place = resume.mode=='loop' && loop_resume_enabled() && checkpoint_enabled(); otherwise run stage 1 exactly as today (downgrade, logged with closed token loop_resume_downgraded; never a refusal, so a switch skew between gateway and executor cannot strand a continue).
 2. consume_for_resume(): the existing first half of prepare_resume, factored out. It makes the ConsumeApproval RPC with approval_id, org, run, hint step_id, hint fingerprint and the claim token. It requires consumed || (already_consumed && same_claim), checks authority_from_proto(snapshot).digest() == snapshot.digest, checks the tool set matches names, checks the approved tool is in the snapshot and the hints agree, and checks releasable(tool). Output is a Consumed value. All refusals here are fatal and unchanged (approval_snapshot_mismatch, approval_action_mismatch, not_releasable, continuation_already_consumed).
 3. effective_authority(snapshot_authority, req): the authority refusals (table C) run BEFORE the claim, so a refusal never takes the lease.
 4. ClaimLoopCheckpoint{run_id, pause_ref=approval_id, claim_token}, classified per A.
 5. Fold checks (each failure is a RestoreFailure, i.e. fallback): LoopFoldV1::from_bytes (version, size); fold.run_id==req.run_id; claimed.kind=='pause' and fold.pending.kind==Approval with pause_ref==approval_id, step_id==consumed.step_id and call==consumed.tool_name; the fold's pending FoldCall arguments digest equals the digest of consumed.tool_input_json (the descriptor stays the only source of what runs; the fold copy is only cross-checked); if resume.action_fingerprint is set it equals fold.pending.action_fingerprint; authority digest equality across claimed.authority_digest, fold.authority.digest() and snapshot.digest (if different: a fold wider than the snapshot is fatal authority_widened via narrows(), otherwise fallback); prompt_digest (D); round structure (E).
 6. Ledger read, only if some call is dangling (not completed, not the pending call): one ListToolActions for the action ids derived from the fold step ids. Pause folds normally have none, so this is mostly for pre_effect/round folds. A read failure is a fallback (ledger_unavailable). Stage 1 never re-runs dangling calls, so a fallback after a failed ledger read cannot duplicate an effect.
 7. Decide with closers::decide (D/E below). Build the seed: messages=fold.messages, counters, seeded InferResponse built from round_in_flight, per-call resolutions, and the ApprovedRelease for the pending call under its NEW step id.
 8. apply_authority(&mut req, effective): overwrite req.autonomy_rung, min_privacy_tier, plan_mode, mode, max_rounds with the effective values (run_rounds reads all of them from ctx.req). Skip publish_plan_transition as stage 1 does. Heartbeat as usual.
 9. run_rounds with the in-place seed. The S6 pre_effect hook saves before phase-2 dispatch (rule in A); a save failure is the typed refusal resume_checkpoint_unavailable.
10. Later saves continue at expected_seq chaining from the claimed seq. Terminalization purges the fold (S4). Nothing here closes the fold.

C. AUTHORITY: what is compared and the refusal table
Sources: P = paused authority (fold.authority, proven equal to the approval snapshot by digest); R = what the /continue request states. The gateway builds /continue with placeholders (sse.rs continue_run: mode 'ask', min_privacy_tier 0, space_id '', provider_hint '', tools empty, autonomy_rung from the per-replica grant store or UNSPECIFIED, max_rounds from env). So a request field counts as STATED only when it is not the neutral value: rung != UNSPECIFIED, floor > 0, plan_mode == true, max_rounds > 0. The effective authority starts from P and takes only stated narrowings. The loop runs under it.
| dimension | request-stated value | comparator | outcome |
| mode | req.mode ignored (gateway sends the placeholder 'ask'); effective = P.mode | Authority::narrows gains a mode rank: deny 0 < ask 1 < auto 2, unknown 3 | fold mode wider than snapshot mode: Refuse authority_widened; otherwise nothing to refuse |
| rung | req.autonomy_rung if != UNSPECIFIED | rung rank, with unspecified/unknown ranked 3 (widest), see risks | request rung wider than P: Refuse authority_widened; narrower: used; UNSPECIFIED: keep P (this fixes the fail-open that existed because rung_rank(unspecified)=0) |
| plan_mode | true if the request says so | narrows(): !P.plan_mode or R.plan_mode | false is 'not stated' and P stays; a request cannot switch plan mode off |
| tool_names | req.tools ignored; the set is the snapshot's | subset of the snapshot's | the released tool not in the set: fatal approval_snapshot_mismatch (existing); a fold tool set not a subset of the snapshot's: authority_widened |
| space_id | req.space_id | must equal P.space_id | different: Refuse authority_space_mismatch (gateway sends '' so any Space run is refused, consistent with DEC-06 continue_space_scope_unsupported) |
| min_privacy_tier | req if > 0 | R >= P | lower non-zero: Refuse authority_widened; higher: used; 0: keep P (the loop currently sends req.min_privacy_tier on every Infer, so without apply_authority the floor drops to 0 on continue) |
| provider_hint | req.provider_hint | must equal P | different: Refuse authority_route_mismatch (a pinned run cannot continue because the gateway cannot send the connection id) |
| max_rounds | req resolved | effective = min(resolved R, resolved P), never a refusal | silently the smaller; compare RESOLVED values (0 means DEFAULT_MAX_ROUNDS, capped at MAX_ROUNDS_CEILING) |
Refusals are fatal: no fallback, because stage 1 would run with the same stated request values. The refusal wording is closed tokens only, via failed_precondition. Apply the same effective_authority(snapshot, req) to stage 1 (it has no fold) so stage 1 stops running under the request's rung and floor.

D. prompt_digest
- Computed over: blake3 with domain tag 'mp.prompt.v1', length-prefixed, over (1) the text of compose_system_prompt(allowlist), the platform preamble plus tool guidance, which is what this build composes for the offered tool names; (2) the offered tool definitions (name, description, parameters_json), sorted by name. NOT over the skill-block system message (per-run, keyed by goal), the goal, authored instructions or history (WS02 content), or anything else in the fold.
- Where stored: LoopFoldV1.prompt_digest (field already exists, #[serde(default)]); S6 computes it on every save via mp_contracts::loop_fold::prompt_digest(system_prompt, tools:&[(&str,&str,&str)]). No new column and no proto change. An empty or missing digest counts as a mismatch.
- Why this and not 'the fold's own system message': at resume the digest is recomputed from the CURRENT BUILD'S compose_system_prompt over the SNAPSHOT'S tool names and tool definitions. A mismatch means the platform prompt or the tools changed since the pause. Resuming under the old prompt would bypass a prompt hardening, so the loop falls back to stage 1, which composes the current prompt. A digest over the fold's own text would prove only self-consistency.
- Also check structurally: fold.messages[0].role=='system'.

E. LEDGER STATUS FEED (decision) AND ROUND REBUILD
Decision: ADD ListToolActions (read-only, digest-only). Using only the fold's recorded outcomes is insufficient: the fold is written before dispatch (pre_effect), so the crash window between reserve and finalize exists only in the ledger. Pause folds usually have no dangling call, because pause_for_approval runs after all of phase 2 and 3, so the RPC is skipped there.
- The released call and any redispatched call always run under a NEW step id (resumed_step_id = 's{N}.' + original step id, N = fold.segment_no+1), hence a NEW ledger action id. This matters because the paused call's own row is 'not_run' (finalize maps awaiting_approval to not_run), and reserving again under the same action id would leave the row not_run after the call completed (finalize would fail with already_exists, and closers would later treat an executed effect as redispatchable). Retries of the same resume compute identical new ids, so effect::reserve's created=false (AlreadyReserved) catches a second attempt. That is the second-line guard.
- For each dangling call (no completed record, not the pending call): row = lookup(action_id_for(original step_id)); identity check: row.tool==call.name and, when both exist, row.args_digest==args_digest_of(call.arguments_json) (mismatch is RestoreFailure LedgerIdentityMismatch); DanglingCall{tool_name, class: effect_class_of(name,args) (or row.effect_class if present), ledger: ledger_status_from_row(row.status), ledger_was_on: true when the fold records it, has_output: false, workspace_available: req.space_id.is_empty() (a Space run is refused earlier; unverified)} -> closers::decide: Keep (not reachable without output), Redispatch (becomes a dispatch slot under a new step id) or Close(kind) (becomes a resolved slot whose error text is closer_text(kind, tool); tool name only, never arguments).
- Completed entries that have output keep it verbatim (resolved slot, not re-recorded: record_tool_step already ran when they completed, so no duplicate STEP_COMPLETED).
- REBUILD of the interrupted round (identical to what the uninterrupted loop appends): messages = fold.messages (the history BEFORE the round, post tier-1 compaction); response = InferResponse{content: assistant_content, tool_calls: calls in ORIGINAL order, stop_reason:'tool_use'} fed through run_rounds as the seeded round (exactly like stage 1's seeded_round, via a new enum RoundSeed{Segment(InferResponse), InPlace(Box<InPlaceSeed>)}). In phase 1, a call with a resolution becomes CallSlot::Rejected(ToolStepResult) (the existing 'already has a result' variant: no dispatch, no record_tool_step, in the outcomes in call order). A dispatchable call keeps going through the gates (allowlist, rung under the effective authority, schema, duplicate-retrieval with attempted_retrievals restored) with its step id taken from the seed instead of step_seq+=1. After phase 3 the loop appends assistant(content) when non-empty, then user(format_tool_context(outcomes in call order, closers included)): byte-identical to the uninterrupted path.
- rounds_executed is NOT incremented again: fold.rounds_executed counts rounds STARTED including the open one (contract S6 must follow when round_in_flight is Some). Restore rounds_executed = fold.rounds_executed - 1 so the loop's own top-of-loop += 1 re-counts that same round once (the round-budget check passes even when the open round was the last). Restore delegated_rounds, step_seq, children_started, grounded, compaction_triggered and attempted_retrievals from the fold.
- Validation (RestoreFailure RoundInvalid): round_in_flight present; 1 <= calls <= 64; call ids non-empty and unique; pending step_id is the step_id of exactly one call; each completed entry resolves to exactly one call by call_id (new field) else step_id; rounds_executed >= 1.

F. CLAIM TOKEN AND PARALLEL /continue (200 vs 409)
- Today (sse.rs continue_run) consume runs in execution-core AFTER the SSE 200 is open, so the loser of a race would get 200 plus an error frame. New: the gateway calls ConsumeApproval (user bearer, same RPC, org from verified claims) BEFORE agentic_run_stream. Mapping: consumed or same_claim: proceed; already_consumed && !same_claim: 409 continuation_already_consumed; NotFound: 404 approval_not_found; approval_not_granted, approval_expired, approval_not_resumable: 409 with that code. execution-core's own consume is then a same_claim replay, so the claim token is passed through unchanged.
- LAYER THAT GUARANTEES: the session-core Postgres UPDATE (single row, serialised by the row lock): exactly one statement returns the row. The gateway only surfaces it as HTTP; the executor re-checks it (replay); the fold claim and the ledger created flag are the second-line guards.
- Two parallel calls with DISTINCT tokens: one 200 stream and one 409 JSON. Two with the SAME token (a retry of one click): both pass consume; the executor's claim refuses the second with claim_held, so it is a 200 stream whose first frame is a typed error continue_in_progress, not an HTTP 409. No double execution either way. Same-token duplicates on a stage-1 segment have no fold lease; the reserve created=false guard covers effectful calls when the ledger is on.
- continue_preflight keeps requiring approval.continuation_mode == 'loop' (the S2 meaning, 'loop-owned'). Stage selection is AgentResume.mode only. Do NOT implement the S6 plan wording 'approval created in segment mode when the pause fold cannot save': nothing reads 'segment' on the approval and continue_preflight would refuse it. S6 should save the pause fold AFTER create_approval (it needs the approval id as pause_ref; CreateApprovalRequest.client_approval_id is empty today so session-core mints it, and the plan text 'pause before CreateApproval' cannot hold) and tolerate a failed fold save by leaving the loop-owned approval as is; /continue then falls back to stage 1.

G. GATEWAY LOOP vs SEGMENT
- mode = resume_mode_for(loop_resume_enabled(), detail.resumable) -> 'loop' only when the gateway's EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED is true AND RunDetail.resumable (the S4 leftover being built in parallel). Required semantics of resumable: a run_loop_checkpoints row exists with state in ('paused','parked') (or resuming with an expired lease), the run's retention is persistent and SESSION_CORE_LOOP_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED is on. It is a hint, not a promise: execution-core decides at claim time, and a mismatch (for example pause_ref) falls back, so a wrong hint costs a fallback and nothing else.
- The gateway no longer hard-codes segment_no: 2. execution-core derives the segment (see risks).

H. SWITCH
EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED, default false, read by both execution-core and model-gateway (compose: execution-core and model-gateway env, '${EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED:-false}', beside AGENT_CONTINUE_AFTER_APPROVAL_ENABLED at deploy/docker-compose.yml ~1042). Parsed with the loop_fold strictness (1/true/on/yes) via mp_contracts::loop_fold::loop_resume_from. Needs AGENT_CONTINUE_AFTER_APPROVAL_ENABLED, EXECUTION_LOOP_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED (S6) and SESSION_CORE_LOOP_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED (S4). With it off, mode 'loop' behaves exactly as 'segment' (stage 1).

I. ZDR AND CREDENTIALS
No new persisted content. ZDR run: refused at the gateway (continuation_gate), at execution-core (agent_run), at consume and at claim (refuse_zdr_continuation, run_owner_tx retention check). Waived runs: claim refuses with DURABLE_MUTATION_FORBIDDEN, which is fatal. ListToolActions returns status, class, digests, tool name and closed_by only, refuses a ZDR caller, and hides rows with zdr=true. Closer sentences name only the tool. Logs carry closed reason codes and counts only, never fold text, arguments or outputs. The claim token is stored as a hash; bearers are minted fresh per /continue and never put in the fold.

Nothing else in claim/save/close changes (save already clears the claim and resets state).

risks: EXISTING GAP (stage 1, found while reading): run_agent_with_route uses req.autonomy_rung, req.min_privacy_tier and req.plan_mode for every gate and every Infer, and the gateway's /continue sends the grant-store rung (UNSPECIFIED on a replica without the grant, which check_autonomy_rung treats as 'no graded constraint'), floor 0 and plan false. So a stage-1 continue can run with a weaker rung and privacy floor than the run paused with. The fix (apply_authority from the snapshot) is in this slice because stage 2 shares it; if the lead wants S7 smaller, ship the stage-1 fix as its own commit first.

EXISTING GAP: Authority::narrows ranks 'unspecified' (and unknown labels) as the narrowest rung, but UNSPECIFIED is fail-open. Fixed by rank 3 in step 1; any other caller of narrows must be re-read (none found besides tests).

EXISTING GAP: gateway continue sets segment_no: 2 and prepare_resume uses s2. for every continuation, so a second pause then continue in one run reuses 's2.tool_1_approved' and collides on ledger action ids (reserve ignored created=false, so the collision is silent for identical calls and 'already_exists' for different ones). Fixed by next_segment_no(consumed.step_id) for stage 1 and fold.segment_no+1 for stage 2.

EXISTING GAP: pause_for_approval gives continuation_mode 'loop' to every non-ZDR pause when AGENT_CONTINUE_AFTER_APPROVAL_ENABLED is on, including book_shipment, tickets.create, browser_agent and subagent.* which stage 1 refuses as not_releasable after burning the approval, and which the cold worker skips because the mode is non-empty: the approval is stranded. One-predicate fix in this slice (cold mode when !releasable).

S6 CONTRACT DRIFT RISK: S7 depends on S6 writing the fold the way the plan says. Points where the plan text does not hold and need S6's agreement: (a) 'pause fold before CreateApproval' cannot carry the approval id as pause_ref because session-core mints it; S6 must save after create_approval (or pre-mint client_approval_id); (b) 'if the pause fold cannot save the approval is created in segment mode' must not be built (nothing reads it and continue_preflight refuses non-'loop'); (c) rejected calls have no step id, hence the new call_id; (d) rounds_executed must include the open round; (e) the S6 pre_effect hook must also run for the resumed round. If S6 has already merged without these, step 5 adapts, but the fold shape contract must be pinned with a golden test in mp-contracts.

ERROR CLASSIFICATION RISK: classifying a claim transport error as a fallback relies on 'a fallback only runs the consume-gated call'. If a future change lets stage 1 re-run dangling calls, that argument breaks and ambiguous claim errors would need to become refusals.

STRANDED APPROVAL: consume burns the click before the later checks. A crash or a fatal refusal after consume leaves the run paused with a spent approval; recovery is a same-token retry (works) or the S8 park TTL / outcome_unknown (a different token is refused). The SPA must reuse one claim token per approval_id; today the claim token is caller-supplied (orchestration-client.ts continueRun takes it as an argument) and there is no UI caller yet.

SAME-TOKEN CONCURRENCY ON STAGE 1: a duplicate of the same token passes consume twice and nothing fences the segments except the ledger created=false guard, which covers effectful calls only when EXECUTION_EFFECT_LEDGER_ENABLED is on. Stage 2 is fenced by the fold lease plus the pre_effect supersede save.

LEASE WINDOW: if the first pre_effect save is skipped by a future refactor, the 120 s lease becomes the only fence for a long-running released call. The test the_released_call_is_not_dispatched_until_the_pre_effect_fold_is_saved pins it.

Hot-file churn: agent.rs (run_rounds seed, prepare_resume split, hot spot called out in plan) and sse.rs are LIVE-modified hot spots; rebase on S6's LoopState refactor before merging step 5 (the seed handling assumes S6's local state names).

Compaction idempotence is assumed: run_rounds calls clear_stale_tool_results at the top of the resumed round on messages already cleared once at the original round top. It replaces payload text with a short notice and picks stale indices by budget, so it should be a no-op the second time; the equality test must include a budget-pressure variant to prove it.

Closers for ledger-off folds: with the ledger off at pause time a missing row proves nothing, so ledger_was_on must come from the fold (S6 should record effect_ledger in extensions); without it the resume must assume off, which closes more effects than needed (safe direction).

Prompt drift on every deploy: a rolling deploy that changes compose_system_prompt makes every in-flight pause fall back to stage 1 (safe, but stage 1's brief is empty today, so the model loses the interrupted round's results). Mitigation (optional, deferred): on PromptDrift with a readable fold, seed the fallback brief from the fold's recorded results through frame_brief.

Gateway pre-consume widens the gateway's role (it now calls ConsumeApproval). The RPC is already user-bearer and org-scoped, execution-core's consume becomes an idempotent replay, and nothing new is persisted; the gateway never sees the fold.

Proto: add-only fields; go/gen does not contain the S4 loop-checkpoint RPCs (grep found none), so no Go regeneration is expected, unverified for ListToolActions. Run buf breaking if the repo has it wired.
invariants: ConsumeApproval is the single authority gate: one approval releases one call once; every other mechanism is a second-line guard and none of them can release a call on their own.
Consume happens before claim, and both use the caller's claim token; a refusal that depends on authority happens before the claim so it never takes the lease.
A resume never widens authority: the effective authority is the paused one, narrowed by whatever the request states; a widening request is a typed refusal and never falls back.
In-place resume never dispatches before the claim has been superseded by a saved pre_effect fold.
The released call and every redispatched call run under a new step id and a new ledger action id; an already-reserved effectful action is never run again.
An effectful call whose outcome is unknown is closed with UnknownOutcome and never retried; closer text names the tool only.
The interrupted round is rebuilt as assistant content (when non-empty) then one tool-context message in original call order, and the round is not charged twice.
The approval descriptor, not the fold, is the only source of what the released call is; a fold that disagrees falls back.
Any restore failure after a won consume falls back to stage 1 using the same Consumed value (no second consume RPC); the fold is not closed by the fallback.
ZDR and waived runs never read or write a fold, a claim or a ledger read; nothing new is persisted by this slice.
No bearer, token or claim token is persisted or logged; logs carry closed reason codes only.
EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED off (or the S6 switch off) means 'loop' runs exactly as 'segment'; the default build is byte-identical to today.
